_notes: Ground truth for scoring the baseline (hardcoded selectors) and agent (DOM classifier) against known and held-out sites. 'remove' = AI elements that should be hidden/removed. 'keep' = real content that must NOT be touched (used to catch false positives). 'surface' = elements that should be made more visible if currently buried.

amazon.notes: Amazon renamed Rufus to 'Alexa for Shopping' around May 2026. DOM still uses 'rufus' in ids/classes as of verification date. Widget shown as a disco-style avatar with 'for shopping' label in the nav bar.

zendesk.notes: Swapped in for Notion Help Center - Zendesk sells AI support chatbots as their core product, so their own site is a reliable, guaranteed placement rather than a rollout-dependent feature.

remove.description: AI chatbot widget launcher (lives in an embedded iframe, identified by its accessible title text rather than a class name)
remove.selector_hint: iframe with title matching pattern 'Button to launch messaging window' - a strong semantic/aria signal, more durable than a CSS class since it's plain-English accessibility text describing the element's purpose
remove.raw_html: <title>Button to launch messaging window, 2 unread messages</title> (found inside an iframe on the page, wrapping an SVG speech-bubble icon)

surface.description: Human contact / 'talk to a human' link, if buried behind the chatbot
